instruction: Use Chrome to open the Google Scholar page for the third author named on the paper.

command: import pyautogui; import time; pyautogui.hotkey('f11'); time.sleep(0.5); pyautogui.click({SCREEN_WIDTH_HALF}, {SCREEN_HEIGHT_HALF}); time.sleep(0.5); pyautogui.scroll(-40)

metadata.explanation: Task variation asking to find the third author's (Linxi Fan) Google Scholar page. Linxi (Jim) Fan is listed as the third author from Stanford University. Uses existing Chrome getters and metrics - no custom functions needed. The expected Google Scholar user ID is wT4hH7IAAAAJ (Linxi Fan's verified Scholar ID).

llm_judge_reasons: Getter function (get_active_url_from_accessTree) correctly extracts the active tab URL from the accessibility tree and adds the https:// prefix
Metric function (is_expected_url_pattern_match) correctly uses regex search to match all expected patterns in the URL
Expected patterns are semantically correct: 'https://scholar.google.com/citations' verifies navigation to Google Scholar, and 'user=wT4hH7IAAAAJ' verifies the specific third author (Linxi Fan)
Complete coverage: evaluator checks both that the user navigated to Google Scholar citations AND that the correct author ID is present in the URL
Logical correctness: metric requires ALL patterns to match, which is appropriate for this task
Practical feasibility: getter can extract active URL, metric can perform regex matching without issues
